title: Review: Particles, isotopes and relative atomic mass; The mole and Avogadro constant; Mass spectrometry of elements; Mass spectrometry and IR of molecules; Ionisation energies
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM01#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM01#N.9, AN01#N.13, AS02#N.13, AN01#N.17c, AM01#N.5a, AN01#N.6, AS01#N.5a, AS02#N.6a, AS05#N.7a, AM01#N.3a, AN01#N.4, AS01#N.7a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass-to-charge ratio
items.clue: The quantity written m/z, plotted on the x-axis of the spectrum.

items.label: Mass spectrometer
items.clue: Instrument that turns particles into positive ions and sorts them.

items.label: Relative abundance
items.clue: Shown by peak height: how much of each isotope an element contains.

items.label: Mole
items.clue: The unit of the quantity n; one of these of CO₂ contains three of atoms.

questions.stem: A one-carat diamond is pure carbon with a mass of 0.200 g. About how many carbon atoms does it contain? Data: Ar C 12.0; N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: n = 0.200 g ÷ the molar mass of C = 0.0167 mol. N = 0.0167 mol × N_A = 1.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Compound Q, C₃H₆O, absorbs strongly at 1725 cm⁻¹ and does not absorb between 3200 and 3600 cm⁻¹. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Q contains C=O and no O–H, so it is an aldehyde or a ketone.
Q contains a C=C bond, so it is prop-2-en-1-ol, CH₂=CHCH₂OH.
Q is an alcohol, since its single O atom must be in an O–H group.
Q must be propanone, since only ketones absorb near 1725 cm⁻¹.

questions.explanation: 1725 cm⁻¹ is a C=O band. No broad band at 3200–3600 rules out an alcohol O–H. With one O atom, Q is propanal or propanone.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of gallium shows two peaks from 1+ ions: m/z 69 (height 100) and m/z 71 (height 66.4). What is the relative atomic mass of gallium given by these data?
Compound X has its molecular ion at m/z 60 and a fragment peak at m/z 45. Its IR spectrum shows a strong absorption at 1710 cm⁻¹ and a very broad absorption from 2500 to 3000 cm⁻¹. What is X?
questions.explanation: Mr = 60; C=O at 1710 cm⁻¹ plus a very broad acid O–H. m/z 45 is COOH⁺, after loss of CH₃ (60 − 45 = 15).

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Mr of carbon dioxide, CO₂ = 44.0 g mol⁻¹'. Which comment on this statement is correct?

options.text: It is correct: Mr and molar mass are one and the same quantity.
The unit is wrong: Mr is the mass of one molecule in grams.
The unit is wrong: Mr is measured in atomic mass units.
The unit is wrong: Mr is a ratio of masses, with no unit.

questions.explanation: Mr compares a CO₂ molecule with 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom; units cancel. M(CO₂) = 44.0 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: A compound gives a molecular ion at m/z = 58.0417 in a high-resolution mass spectrum. Use ¹H 1.0078, ¹²C 12.0000, ¹⁴N 14.0031, ¹⁶O 15.9949. What is its molecular formula?
An ion X³⁺ contains 23 electrons and 30 neutrons. Which nuclear symbol represents this ion? (Each symbol is written with its superscript first and its subscript second.)
questions.explanation: Protons = 23 + 3 = 26 = Z. Mass number = 26 + 30 = 56. (X is iron.)

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?
How does the first ionisation energy generally change across Period 3 from sodium to argon, and why?

options.text: It decreases, as the fixed pull of the nucleus is shared among more and more electrons.
It decreases, as the atoms get larger because more electrons are added along the period.
It increases, as atoms closer to a full outer shell resist losing any of their outer electrons.
It increases, as the nuclear charge rises while the outer electrons have similar shielding.

questions.explanation: Nuclear charge +11 to +18; the electron removed is in the third shell, with similar shielding. 496 → 1521 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in 0.500 mol of water, H₂O? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
Methyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₃ (Mr = 102), gives a peak at m/z 71. Which neutral fragment was lost to form this ion?
questions.explanation: 102 − 71 = 31: OCH₃. Losing the methoxy group leaves CH₃CH₂CH₂CO⁺ (m/z 71), a sign of a methyl ester.

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: At the same temperature the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average. Diffusion rate is a physical property.
